result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with sidewalks on both sides and a marked zebra crosswalk at a side street intersection. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The width of the travel lanes and the overall roadway may encourage vehicle speeds higher than appropriate for a residential area.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb can block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Speed Cushions
interventions.description: Implement speed cushions or humps to physically reduce vehicle speeds in this residential corridor.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Add high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

result.summary: This residential street features narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to the roadway without a protective buffer. While the walking surface appears intact, the presence of on-street parking and the lack of marked crossings or traffic calming measures create a basic but unprotected pedestrian environment.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is narrow and placed directly against the curb, providing no physical or psychological separation between pedestrians and moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the far side of the street where the sidewalk meets the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars along the curb line can block the sight lines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children, who might step into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Vehicles parked along the curb on the far side of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at nearby intersections to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce the crossing distance across the street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip with street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical buffer and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The street is a wide, straight residential road with sidewalks on both sides but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. Parallel parking on both sides creates potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Wide, straight roadway
hazards.description: The long, straight, and relatively wide pavement encourages higher vehicle speeds in a residential context.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street can hide pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to physically slow traffic in this residential area.

result.summary: This residential street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, separated from the roadway by a grass buffer strip. The environment includes visible curb ramps and marked crosswalks at the intersection, though the presence of on-street parking may impact visibility for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner can obscure the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right-hand curb approaching the intersection

hazards.name: Wide Corner Radius
hazards.description: The wide curve at the intersection corner may allow vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom right corner of the image

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the pedestrian crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing crosswalk markings to a high-visibility continental pattern to increase driver awareness.
